violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) in the 1DR Hot Box, left of rotating grill: leftover beef rib (121f)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC INSTRUCTED STAFF TO REHEAT ALL LEFTOVER BEEF RIBS TO 165f BEFORE PUTTING IT IN THE HOT BOX. STAFF MOVED THE BEEF RIB TO THE GRILL TO REHEAT TO 165f. THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. ENFORCEMENT MAY BE WARRANTED.

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers of garlic were observed reused for the storage of prepared food throughout the kitchen
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. REPLACE GARLIC CONTAINERS WITH NSF APPROVED FOOD STORAGE CONTAINERS.

violations.title: Fixed Equipment, Properly Spaced and Sealed
violations.observation: The hand sink by the dish washing area was observed loose and not sealed to the wall.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment that is fixed because it is not easily movable shall be installed so that it is: 1) spaced to allow access for cleaning along the sides, behind, and above the equipment, 2) spaced from adjoining equipment, walls, and ceilings a distance of not more than 1 millimeter or one thirty-second inch, and 3) sealed to adjoining equipment or walls if the equipment is exposed to spillage or seepage. SECURE AND RESEAL HAND SINK.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): elevate boxes of Raw meat off of the floor
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. DISCONTINUE USING MILK CRATES BECAUSE THEY ARE NOT EASILY CLEANABLE. USE DUNNAGE RACKS OR OTHER NSF APPROVED SHELVING

violations.title: Records, Parasite Destruction, Farm-Raised
violations.observation: The following farm-raised fish served raw or partially cooked were observed without a written statement from the supplier stating that the fish were raised and fed according to 3-402.11(B)(3): salmon. EHS observed a parasite destruction letter that did not list the specific fish that was subjected to parasite destruction.
violations.corrective_action: Contact your fish supplier and ask for a written statement stating that the fish were raised in net pens if in open water OR land-based operations AND fed formulated feed that contains no live parasites. FAX a copy of this letter to your inspector and keep this statement on site at the food establishment for 90 days beyond the time of service of the fish. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO CONTACT THE FISH SUPPLIER FOR AN UPDATED PARASITE DESTRUCTION LETTER THAT SPECIFICALLY STATES THE FISH NAME. PLEASE PROVIDE EHS WITH THE REQUIRED DOCUMENT BY THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Food Thermometer, Repair and Calibration
violations.observation: The food temperature measuring device was found out of calibration in the range of use. EHS observed PIC’s food probe thermometer reading 2 degrees higher than EHS’s calibrated food probe thermometer
violations.corrective_action: Food thermometers shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. It is suggested that food thermometers be calibrated at least once a week in a cup completely filled with ice and cold water to a temperature of 32F or calibrated in a pot of boiling water at 212F. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO GET A NEW FOOD PROBE THERMOMETER. PLEASE MAKE THIS CORRECTION BY THE FOLLOW UP.
